subject: Proof of enforcement: SAML/SCIM/RBAC traces and privilege activation samples (SOC 2 request)
messages:
From: Jason Miller <jason.miller@acmehealth.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: security-team@acmehealth.com
Date: Tue, 1 Sep 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Evidence request: enforcement traces for SOC 2 control testing

Hi Dylan —

As part of our SOC 2 testing window next month, the auditors asked us to get concrete enforcement traces showing that RBAC/SCIM/SAML controls are actually enforced:

- A short sample of SAML assertions showing attributes used for authorization (no passwords)
- SCIM sync deltas for a 3–5 day window to show provisioning/deprovisioning behavior
- RBAC role snapshot for a point-in-time (owner and member lists)
- Any privilege-activation traces (JIT/admin elevation requests) during the same window

Can Redwood provide redacted samples and a short explanation of where these artifacts come from and how to read them? Our auditors prefer examples with timestamps and correlation IDs.

Goal: deliver samples + a one-page narrative by 2026-09-10 if possible. Please let me know if that timeline is feasible and what you’ll provide.

Thanks,
Jason
Jason Miller
Lead Security Analyst — Acme Health
security-team@acmehealth.com

--
Attachment: (none)
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Jason Miller <jason.miller@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Sep 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Evidence request: enforcement traces for SOC 2 control testing

Jason —

Thanks for the clear ask. We can assemble a compact evidence package that meets the auditors’ preference for timestamps and correlation IDs. Proposed deliverables (by 2026-09-09):

1) SAML assertion sample (CSV) with assertion time, subject, audience, persistent identifier and the authorization attributes we evaluate.
2) SCIM delta snapshot for a 72-hour window (redacted UPNs) showing create/update/delete events and the deltas that drove role changes.
3) RBAC point-in-time role membership export (CSV) with role owners flagged.
4) Privilege activation traces (zipped trace files) for any admin elevation flows during Aug 25–Aug 31.
5) One-page narrative + a short walkthrough recording (link) explaining how to interpret correlation IDs and TTL behavior.

A couple quick clarifying questions:
- Do the auditors require raw assertion XMLs or are parsed CSV samples sufficient?
- For SCIM, is a 72-hour sample acceptable or do they want a longer window?

Laura / Grace — I’m looping you in to confirm the production locations and to capture the redaction steps.

Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Security & Compliance Ops — Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Jason Miller <jason.miller@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Sep 2026 12:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Evidence request: enforcement traces for SOC 2 control testing

Jason —

72 hours should be fine for a sample, auditors typically want representative evidence rather than entire logs. We will:

- Deliver parsed CSVs for readability; we can include one raw SAML assertion (anonymized) if they insist.
- Redact PII and replace UPNs with deterministic pseudonyms (e.g. user-001).
- Provide a mapping file that shows pseudonym => internal id (delivery only to Acme security).

If that works, we’ll target 2026-09-09 COB for the package. I’ll coordinate with Grace on the export window and redaction.

Laura Bennett
Account Director — Redwood Inference
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Jason Miller <jason.miller@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 2 Sep 2026 09:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Evidence request: enforcement traces for SOC 2 control testing

Hi Jason —

Technical notes from the exports team (to help auditors map fields):

- SAML: we will pull assertion metadata from our assertion store. The sample CSV columns: assertion_time, issuer, subject_id, audience, authn_instant, attributes(role, entitlements), correlation_id. We will remove NameID email values and replace with pseudonyms. File: 2026-08-saml-assertions-sample.csv (attached).

- SCIM: we can produce a scim-delta-sync-snapshot-20260831.json containing the 72-hour window of delta events and the associated change tokens. Events include created_by, timestamp, attribute_deltas. Sensitive fields redacted.

- RBAC: rbac-role-snapshot-20260831.csv will show role_id, role_name, owner_principal (pseudonym), member_count, last_changed_by, last_changed_at.

- Privilege activation: our JIT elevational flow produces a trace entry with request_id, requesting_principal, approver, start_ts, end_ts, outcome. We’ll bundle matching traces into privilege-activation-traces-aug-2026.zip. If auditors need raw stack traces for a specific request_id we can elevate.

- Policy enforcement narrative / workback: policy-enforcement-workback-plan-ACME.pdf (attached) explains how enforcement decisions are made, kernel-level checks, and how prefix caching interacts with authorization for API tokens.

A couple of practical items:
- We’ll redact and pseudonymize at-rest identifiers before delivery.
- We will deliver files via our secured Share link and also provide a short walkthrough recording. Link will be included in the package.

Grace O'Connor
Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference

Attachments: 2026-08-saml-assertions-sample.csv; scim-delta-sync-snapshot-20260831.json; rbac-role-snapshot-20260831.csv; privilege-activation-traces-aug-2026.zip; policy-enforcement-workback-plan-ACME.pdf

Dylan / Grace —

This looks good. CSVs + one raw SAML XML (anonymized) is preferred. 72-hour SCIM sample is acceptable. Auditor ask: can we get the package by 2026-09-09 morning PST? They will review and may request 1–2 follow-ups but the bulk of the work will be done.

Please deliver to the HubSpot ticket (link) or via the secure Share link you mentioned. Thanks for the fast turnaround.

Jason
